messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty auto-page PD-67891 — prometheus scrape job 'prometheus-exporter-scrape' missing metrics for 3 targets for 2m. Severity: P2. Paging eng-sre.
Maya: acked PD-67891, I'm taking lead. oncall note: multiple pages (PD-67892 also fired) — looks like duplicate alerts.
Sam: seeing both PD numbers. dashboards show exporter metrics drop to 0 starting ~3732123300. Not seeing API 5xxs on the exporter svc, but scrape responses are empty.
Trent: checking exporter pods now. `kubectl -n monitoring get pods -l app=node-exporter` shows a couple in CrashLoopBackOff. grabbing logs.
Trent: logs from exporter-7f8c9: `2026-03-15T01:10:12Z error: failed to scrape /metrics: read tcp 10.0.4.12:9100->10.0.6.10:443: i/o timeout`
Luis: heads up - at the same time I'm seeing consumer lag grow on topic `logs-ingest-backfill` (consumer group: prometheus-scrape-proxy). lag +120k in last 5m. Could be downstream S3/backpressure or network egress saturation.
Amber: any immediate customer impact? Any alerts firing other than prometheus-scrape?
Sam: internal alerting graphs with zeros will suppress app-level alerts, but external customer metrics ingestion for a small subset (region eu-west-1) shows delayed ingestion. Customers may see delayed time-series but not data loss so far.
Maya: running quick health checks on nodes: `ssh node-monitor-12 -- sudo ifstat 1 1` shows egress at ~95% on nic eth0 for a couple nodes.
Maya: hypothesis: noisy exporters + scrape fanout = network saturation causing scrape timeouts -> duplicate PD pages + backlog on kafka.
Trent: quick mitigation: throttling scrape concurrency and adding a rate-limit on the scrape-proxy. Applying a temporary SLO patch.
Sam: I'm going to scale the prometheus-scrape proxy deployment from 3 -> 6 to increase parallelism and reduce per-pod latency. `kubectl -n monitoring scale deploy/prometheus-scrape-proxy --replicas=6`
Trent: also reducing scrape_concurrency in prometheus config to 50 from 200 to ease egress. will push via configmap patch.
Maya: applied node-level egress QoS rule to deprioritize internal batch traffic (only for 15m window) — monitoring for effect.
Luis: consumer lag stopped growing after scaling; lag peaked and trending down. looks promising.
incident-bot: PD-67891 acknowledged by Maya. PD-67892 auto-closed as duplicate (linked to PD-67891).
Amber: nice. Are we confident this is remediated or do we need an oncall handoff?
Maya: trending stable, but I want to hand off to night oncall Ravi for 30m watch in case of recurrence. leaving runbook notes in PD and chat.
Ravi: thanks, I'll take watch. please paste the exact commands you ran and the config delta so I can revert if needed.
Sam: commands pasted to PD-67891 log: `kubectl scale`, `kubectl apply -f prometheus-scrape-configmap-patch.yaml` and the QoS iptables script snippet.
Trent: config diff: `- scrape_concurrency: 200` -> `+ scrape_concurrency: 50` (temporary). will raise PR to make rate-limits configurable.
Maya: customer impact note added: partial delays in eu-west-1 metric ingestion for ~10-25m for a small subset of customers; no data loss detected.
Amber: recording incident under postmortem-needed? probably low-sev but duplication + paging noise suggests we should follow up on alert dedupe logic.
Maya: agree — marking for a short postmortem focusing on: 1) why duplicate pages fired (dedupe gap), 2) why egress saturates under scrape fanout, 3) how to auto-throttle scrapes earlier.
Ravi: oncall accepted. I'll monitor dashboards and escalate if PD re-fires.
Maya: leaving channel — will be available on PD if anything pops back up. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: PD-67891 status updated => resolved (acknowledged, mitigation applied).
Ravi: confirmed stable at +10m watch. closing thread for now, will open follow-up ticket for dedupe + QoS tuning. :white_check_mark:
